name: verilog_compiler
content: The code has no compile error. I should give this implementation to the user.

The error in the original code is that `tc` is declared as an `output` (which defaults to a `wire` in Verilog) but is being assigned a value inside an `always` block using a non-blocking assignment (`tc <= ...`). In Verilog, any signal assigned within an `always` block must be declared as a `reg` type.

To fix this, I changed the declaration of `tc` to `output reg tc`.

```verilog
module top_module(
	input clk, 
	input load, 
	input [9:0] data, 
	output reg tc
);

reg [9:0] counter; 
	always @(posedge clk) begin 
		if (load) begin 
			counter <= data; 
		end 
		else if (counter != 0) begin 
			counter <= counter - 1'b1; 
		end 
		tc <= (counter == 0); 
	end 
endmodule
```
